userStories.title: OpenCode Binary Detection and Version Check

userStories.title: OpenCode Server Lifecycle Manager
userStories.description: When RORCA_AGENT=opencode, manage an OpenCode server process that stays warm across stories using the --attach flag. Start the server before the first story, reuse it for all subsequent stories in a run, shut it down after run completes.
acceptanceCriteria: New backend/src/lib/opencode-server.ts manages server lifecycle
start(): spawns 'opencode server' with detached:true, captures server socket/port
attach(): returns --attach flag value for use in story execution
stop(): gracefully terminates server process after run completes or on error
Server PID stored alongside pipeline_runs.pid in DB
If server crashes mid-run, backend attempts one restart before marking run failed
Server startup timeout: 10s before giving up
Logs server stdout/stderr to os.tmpdir()/rorca-opencode-server.log

userStories.title: execution-engine.ts Agent Switching Logic
userStories.description: Update backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts to detect RORCA_AGENT and switch the per-story subprocess accordingly. userStories.title: Story Complexity Scorer — Model Tier Assignment
userStories.description: Analyze each story before spawning its subprocess and assign a ModelTier (haiku | sonnet | opus) based on story complexity signals. Eliminates blind Opus usage for every story — routes cheap work to cheap models.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/complexity-scorer.ts exports score(story) → { tier: 'haiku'|'sonnet'|'opus', score: number, signals: string[] }

Scoring signals: dependsOn depth (+10 per level), acceptanceCriteria count (+5 each), file path patterns (docs/**→-20, src/core/**→+20), story type tag (docs→haiku, test→sonnet, feat→sonnet/opus, architecture→opus)
Keyword detection in description: 'rename'/'update import'/'fix typo' → haiku; 'refactor'/'migrate' → sonnet; 'design'/'architect'/'implement from scratch' → opus
Score thresholds configurable in .rorca/config.json orchestration.thresholds (default: 0-30→haiku, 31-65→sonnet, 66+→opus)
ModelTier maps to actual model IDs per provider in orchestration.cascades config
Scorer runs synchronously before subprocess spawn — adds <10ms overhead
Score + signals logged to WAL event payload for FinOps tracking
Unit tests cover all scoring signals and threshold boundaries

userStories.title: Cascading Escalation Engine
userStories.description: When a story fails on a cheaper model tier, automatically escalate to the next tier and retry. Haiku fails twice → Sonnet. Sonnet fails → Opus. Ensures quality without over-provisioning expensive models upfront.
acceptanceCriteria: Escalation config in .rorca/config.json: orchestration.escalation.maxRetriesOnTier (default: 2), orchestration.escalation.escalateTo mapping
execution-engine.ts tracks retry count per story per tier via run-state.json
On story failure: check retry count vs maxRetriesOnTier — if exceeded, escalate model tier and retry
Escalation chain: haiku → sonnet → opus (stop at opus, no further escalation)
WAL event written on escalation: { type: 'story_escalated', fromTier, toTier, attemptNumber, storyId }
Run View shows escalation indicator in story list: 'Escalated: Haiku→Sonnet (attempt 3)'
Escalation disabled for claude --print subscription path (model fixed at story level, not mid-story)
Escalation adds actual cost for escalated attempts to FinOps tracking
Config option: orchestration.escalation.enabled (default: true) — can disable for predictable billing

userStories.title: Multi-Engine Run Lifecycle Management
userStories.description: Manage the process lifecycle for runs that use multiple execution engines simultaneously. OpenCode server starts conditionally (only when opencode-assigned stories exist), Claude and Codex spawn fresh per story, and rate limit overflows automatically reroute stories to the configured secondary engine rather than halting the run.

Secondary engine fallback configurable in .rorca/config.json: orchestration.fallbackEngine (default: null — disable overflow)

userStories.title: Codex Direction Stack Injection
userStories.description: Codex CLI supports AGENTS.md files for persistent context injection (equivalent to CLAUDE.md for Claude Code). Without this, Codex stories run with zero direction context — no engineering principles, no architecture constraints, no stack-specific guidance.

userStories.title: Tool Capability Gating — Pre-Spawn Compatibility Check
userStories.description: Before routing a story to an execution engine, check whether the story's requirements are compatible with that engine's tool set. Codex lacks webfetch, websearch, native glob, and grep. Stories requiring these tools should warn in the trigger modal and optionally auto-reroute to a capable engine rather than failing silently mid-run.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/src/lib/tool-capability-checker.ts exports check(story, engine) → { compatible: boolean, missingTools: string[], warnings: string[] }

Tool capability matrix defined: claude={ bash, edit, read, write, glob, grep, webfetch, websearch, task, todowrite }, opencode={ bash, edit, read, write, glob, grep, webfetch, websearch }, codex={ bash, edit, read, write }, ollama={ bash, edit, read, write }

Keyword detection in story description + acceptanceCriteria: 'webfetch'/'fetch URL'/'documentation lookup' → requires webfetch; 'find files'/'search codebase' → requires glob/grep; 'subagent'/'parallel' → requires task tool
Trigger modal shows capability warnings per story when detected: 'US-007 uses webfetch — not supported by Codex, will reroute to Claude'
orchestration.capabilityMismatch config in .rorca/config.json: 'warn' (default) | 'reroute' | 'block'
When 'reroute': execution-engine.ts automatically escalates to nearest capable engine before spawn (Codex→OpenCode→Claude)
When 'block': trigger returns 400 with list of incompatible story+engine pairs before run starts
WAL event on capability reroute: { type: 'story_rerouted', reason: 'capability_mismatch', missingTools, fromEngine, toEngine }
Unit tests cover all tool capability matrix entries and all three mismatch handling modes
